text:
infra-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: private-us-east-2/gpu-pool is reporting sustained queue growth > 90% for 7m. Autoscaler attempted 4 node launches, all timed out. Paging @sara (oncall) and @rafael (infra).

sara: ack - looking now. any impacted customers?

infra-bot: Impact: increased 429s and request latency on /v1/generate for customers pinned to private-us-east-2. Recent spike at 23:04 UTC. Autoscaler error: "node provisioning timed out: attach volume failed: InsufficientIPs" (see logs snippet).

rafael: I'm on call standby. throwing up the cluster events now.

neha: paging in support for customer comms. which customers are hitting this?

infra-bot: Top impacted tenants: [acmehealth-prod, ledger-sim, beta-ocr]. AcmeHealth is seeing 15% 429s and backlog >1200 requests.

alex: quick checks: `kubectl get nodes -o wide` shows pool target=12, ready=4, provisioning=0. cloud provider returns quota error on subnet IPs.

rafael: confirmed. VPC ENI pool exhausted in us-east-2-private-subnet-3. New nodes fail to get IPs -> provisioning retries then timeout.

sara: ok, short-term mitigations: 1) enable routing of non-critical traffic to hosted region, 2) evict low-priority queued jobs, 3) increase ephemeral IP quota if possible. Who can do (1)?

alex: I can flip route policy for the next 20m to divert non-enterprise tenants to hosted-us-east-1. doing now.

alex: done: routing rule updated via console. traffic from tags `tier: free` and `tier: beta` -> hosted-us-east-1. Should shave queue by ~30%.

rafael: Trying hotfix to use secondary subnet pool in the VPC. Cloud call required to attach ENI pool. Requesting elevated creds from infra-admin. ETA ~8m.

neha: Messaging AcmeHealth PG: "We’re routing non-critical requests away while we remediate. Observed degraded throughput; team is actively triaging." I'll update twice an hour.

pd-bot: Escalation policy triggered: alert severity P1, paging SRE rotation.

sara: temporary throttling policy: applying reject-rate to new requests from invalid tokens and large-batch jobs to prioritize enterprise traffic. Command:```curl -X POST https://controlplane/api/traffic/rate -d '{"policy":"reject-large-batch","limit":200}'```

alex: applied reject-large-batch policy. verified fewer large jobs entering queue. queue length dropping ~12% in last 90s.

rafael: cloud console shows successful attachment of secondary subnet ENI pool. Starting node-provision attempts again.

infra-bot: Autoscaler attempt #5: node created; kubelet registration succeeded; however several pods returned `ImagePullBackOff` due to ECR rate limits on this private repo.

sara: hmm. ECR throttling on startup causing pod readiness delays — that explains slow scale. mitigation: 1) increase parallel pulls with backoff, 2) pre-warm nodes with stale image, 3) enable fallback model variant smaller image. Who can run pre-warm?

rafael: I'll trigger a pre-warm job: `for i in {1..6}; do ssh node && docker pull repo/redwood-runtime:stable; done` kicking off now.

alex: Pre-warm started. Meanwhile I'm reducing batch size policy on high-throughput routes to reduce per-request resource demand.

neha: CS update sent: "We are seeing provisioning delays caused by IP limits and container registry throttling; steps taken: diverted non-critical traffic, applied throttles to large jobs, pre-warmed nodes. Expected stabilization in 10-20 minutes."

sara: handing off active management to rafael (infra) in 10m — I need to step OOO for an hour. rafael, if you need escalation to platform eng, ping @alex.

rafael: confirmed, taking lead. continuing to monitor. next check-in in 5m.

infra-bot: Note: autoscaler has a backoff window after 6 failed attempts. We bumped to force new attempts; watch for throttled API errors.

pd-bot: Attaching runbook: `runbooks/provisioning/node-ip-exhaustion.md` (link). Reminder: set `enable-burst=true` only if QA has validated fallback.

rafael: nodes registering now, readiness improving. queue down 45% from peak. still some 429s for AcmeHealth but tail latency reduces.

customer-success: AcmeHealth PM acknowledged the mitigation. They asked for RCA and ETA for full restore. I'll collect logs and coordinate on postmortem.

sara: thanks team. Rafael, file incident ticket with cause: VPC ENI/IP exhaustion + ECR rate limits preventing node warmup -> autoscaler timeouts. Include timeline, impacted customers, mitigation steps, and follow-ups (increase IP pool, add image pull caching, and refactor autoscaler retry/backoff heuristics).

rafael: creating incident in tracker now. tags: oncall, infra, provisioning, customer-impact.

alex: follow-ups: 1) add pre-warm to autoscaler lifecycle, 2) add proactive ENI capacity check to scale logic, 3) add hosted fallback for pinned tenants.

sara: handing off officially to rafael. I'm OOO. good work. :thumbsup:

rafael: thanks. I’ll update this thread after postmortem draft. closing active page when queue < 10% and all impacted customers within SLA thresholds.

infra-bot: Incident state: mitigated -> monitoring. Autoscaler recovery confirmed at +18m.

neha: I'll schedule customer follow-up call with AcmeHealth and share incident summary.

rafael: final note for handover: root cause: insufficient IP allocation in private subnet combined with container registry throttles slowing node readiness -> autoscaler gave up. Remediation tasks already created.

sara: copied. thanks everyone.
